threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: When you stop holding doors for people at the station—it's a quick way to spot a newbie. Locals just glide past without a glance.
Last night on the 35, a guy serenaded the whole bus with a ukulele version of 'Wonderwall.' The driver just kept shaking his head, smiling.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: When I realized I was home? Walking past the corner shop, I saw a kid selling hand-painted rocks—genuine Neukölln hustle right there.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: You can hop on a tram after midnight and hear spontaneous karaoke from a group of friends. Only in Kreuzberg do everyday rides turn into impromptu concerts.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know someone’s local when they know the taco truck schedules better than the Muni timetables. That’s dedication!

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: I saw a guy in a suit chase a runaway dog down Market St while trying to catch a bus. That pup really had him running!

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists always think they can walk anywhere, but wait till they hit those steep streets after a few cervezas. It’s a workout just going home!

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell recent arrivals by their confusion at the 'siesta' hours—still trying to shop or eat at 3 PM when everything's closed.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still call it 'the City' instead of 'central London' and ask which bus goes to Dalston. That accent makes you stick out like a sore thumb.
Saw a guy on the 36 last night expertly folding a massive paper map while the rest of us just stared at our phones. No one even asked where he was going.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The moment I saw an old man feeding pigeons under the U-Bahn bridge while a street artist painted a mural behind him. Just a typical Neukölln day.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: You can overhear techno beats at 3 AM while waiting for a bus after a night out. Only in Berlin do the urban sounds blend with the heartbeat of the night.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know someone's from here if they can casually dodge a Muni bus stuck behind a dog on the tracks like it's just another Tuesday.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Just saw a guy serenading the Muni with a ukulele while waiting for the 47—only in SF could that happen amidst the chaos.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think Gràcia's plazas are quiet spots for coffee, but locals know they turn into vibrant markets and music stages on weekends.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can always tell by their bewildered faces when they try to navigate the metro map—especially at L1's Plaça Catalunya during rush hour.
